original_question: Does the reverse-mathematical strength of Milliken's theorem depend on the height of the finite strong trees being colored?
target_in_paper: The Milliken-theorem problem in Dobrinen's 2018 problem list: determine the reverse-mathematical strength of Milliken's tree theorem when restricted to colorings of finite strong subtrees of fixed height n, i.e. whether that strength changes with the height parameter.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right theorem (Milliken's tree theorem), the right metamathematical lens (reverse mathematics), and the key parameter that matters in the later formalization of Dobrinen's problem: the height n of the finite strong subtrees being colored.
missing_details: It should specify the base theory: the reverse-mathematical comparison is over RCA_0.
It should name the fixed-height restriction explicitly, usually denoted MTT^n: Milliken's tree theorem for strong subtrees of height n.
It should state the ambient objects: an infinite finitely branching tree T with no leaves (in the computability-theoretic formalization, computably bounded when discussing computable instances).
It should specify the coloring domain and codomain: a finite coloring f : S^n(T) -> k, where S^n(T) is the set of strong subtrees of T of height n and k >= 1 is finite.
It should make homogeneity explicit: the solution is an infinite strong subtree S of T such that every member of S^n(S) receives the same color under f.
It should say whether the question concerns each fixed n separately or comparison between different n. The paper-faithful version is about the family of principles MTT^n as n varies.
It should avoid the phrase 'finite strong trees being colored' unless it is clarified that one colors finite strong subtrees of a fixed infinite tree, not arbitrary finite trees in isolation.

To match the paper's actual focus, it should highlight the critical comparison between the pair case n = 2 and the higher-height cases n >= 3, rather than leaving 'depend on the height' completely unconstrained.
No algebraic ambient ring/field, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is relevant here; the omitted structure is combinatorial/tree-theoretic rather than algebraic.
refined_question: Over RCA_0, for each fixed n >= 1, what is the reverse-mathematical strength of MTT^n, the restriction of Milliken's tree theorem asserting that for every finite coloring f : S^n(T) -> k of the strong subtrees of height n of an infinite finitely branching tree T with no leaves, there is an infinite strong subtree S of T such that all members of S^n(S) have the same f-color? In particular, does the strength of MTT^n vary with n, especially between the height-2 case and the higher-height cases n >= 3?
justification: The 2018 arXiv item is a short problem list rather than a long technical development, so the draft's core idea has to be sharpened using the standard formalization that later work explicitly says was motivated by Dobrinen's question. That formalization introduces MTT^n as Milliken's tree theorem restricted to strong subtrees of height n, makes precise what the input coloring and homogeneous output subtree are, and shows why the height parameter is exactly the relevant one. The draft is therefore on target, but it is not yet stand-alone because it omits the base theory, the domain of the coloring, the meaning of 'strong tree,' and the quantifier structure. The refined question keeps the draft's intent while restoring the paper-faithful formal content.
